newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African fixed investment slows in Q4 1996.
newsitem.headline: S.African fixed investment slows in Q4 1996.

text.p: South African fixed investment slowed markedly in the latter half of 1996, as did growth in private consumption expenditure, the Reserve Bank said in its latest Quarterly Bulletin.

The rate of growth in aggregate real gross domestic fixed investment (seasonally adjusted and annualised) slowed to just 2.5 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from eight percent in the first quarter, the central bank said.
For the full year, GDFI rose by seven percent, significantly lower than the 10.5 percent estimated for 1995.
Private consumption expenditure also slowed at the end of 1996, registering an increase of 2.5 percent in the fourth quarter after a rate of three to four percent in the first three quarters.
The ratio of gross domestic saving to gross domestic product declined from 17 percent in 1995 to 16.5 percent in 1996.
Savings levels were particularly worrying among private households, the Reserve Bank said. Net savings by households as a ratio of GDP fell to just one percent from 1.5 percent in 1995.

"The very low savings level of the household sector is not only inadequate relative to the economy's investment and growth requirements, but also reveals the short time horizon over which consumers make their spending and saving decisions," it said.
"It also implies a lack of concern among individuals for the need to provide for their old age."
The bulk of private sector savings were concentrated in the corporate sector, it added.
